title: Local descent for a completed coefficient line
statement: Let l be prime, S Noetherian, and L a completed coefficient module. If every pro-etale object admits a covering sieve on whose members L is isomorphic to the regular completed coefficient module, then the underlying constant-coefficient degree-zero object receives at most one map from every complex on which l acts invertibly.

source.place: paragraph (1), local trivialization and descent of derived completeness

proof.text: For an additive category with countable products let P(M)=product_n M and Delta_l(M)=1-l*shift. This is natural in M and additive product-preserving functors carry it to the same operator via the canonical product comparison. If l^e annihilates M, then (l*shift)^e=0, so the finite geometric sum inverts Delta_l(M). Apply this to the additive constant sheaves Z/l^(n+1); forgetting commutative-ring structure commutes with constant sheafification.

The completed coefficient sheaf is the specified ordinary limit of those finite ring sheaves. Forgetting to additive sheaves preserves this limit. The countable-power functor preserves limits (it is the constant-diagram functor followed by a product). Naturality of Delta makes its finite-level inverses compatible; the limit universal property therefore makes Delta invertible on the completed coefficient sheaf. No surjectivity or derived-limit computation is needed here.

Write M for the constant-scalar restriction of L. On a member V of a displayed covering sieve, evaluating the given isomorphism L.over V with the regular module at id_V identifies the additive group M(V) with the completed coefficient ring at V. Evaluation preserves products, so the preceding Delta isomorphism transfers to the evaluation of Delta_l(M) at V. A morphism of sheaves invertible on all members of a covering sieve is invertible globally, by the covering-sieve sheaf limit property. Hence Delta_l(M) is an isomorphism in the ordinary module-sheaf category.

Countable products of constant-coefficient pro-etale module sheaves are exact, using the published source countableAB4Star instance (the constant-ring specialization of exact pro-etale products). K-injective resolutions show that localization Q preserves these products, so the degree-zero single functor also preserves them. For any l-invertible V and f:V->M[0], form g_n=inv(l id_V)^n followed by f. They satisfy l*g_(n+1)=g_n. The product lift g therefore has g;Delta_l(M[0])=0, while Delta_l(M[0]) is invertible. Thus g=0, and its zeroth projection gives f=0. Finally the exact-functor single comparison identifies the requested underlying completed degree-zero object with M[0].
